section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: The Assembler module provides a stateful SWI interface to the Assemble instruction-set library. A caller creates a context for a CPU, supplies values and source lines, and controls the usual one or two assembly passes.
Contexts own their symbols but never own assembled output. The caller supplies the output location, capacity and logical P% at the start of each pass.

section.title: Technical Details
section.p: Contexts are opaque non-zero handles. Source lines are length-delimited plain ASCII and use the syntax accepted by the selected CPU backend. The caller passes every OPT value unchanged to .

Begin the first pass with a null destination and length -1 to measure only, or supply writable memory to retain provisional output. The second-pass call returns the number of forward references encountered in pass one; when this is zero, retained pass-one output is final and replay may be skipped.
Each line is transactional. On failure the output buffer, P%, symbols and pass state remain unchanged. supplies the translated module error, original library classifier and detailed diagnostic.

Values use a 16-byte block containing magic word &41535631, type, signed 32-bit integer and a reserved word. Only integer type 1 is currently supported. The evaluator accepts decimal and &hexadecimal values, identifiers, parentheses, unary plus/minus, arithmetic, MOD, shifts, AND, EOR and OR.

use.p: CPU-specific features are selected later through OPT bits.
Releases all values and assembler symbols owned by the context.

entry.register-use: Output buffer address, or zero for first-pass measurement.
Output capacity, or -1 for first-pass measurement.

exit.register-use: For pass two, number of pass-one forward references; otherwise zero.

use.p: Sets the destination and logical address for the selected pass.
Assembles exactly one source line and advances the context on success.

swi-definition.name: Assembler_Value
swi-definition.description: Reads, writes or deletes a context value

use.p: Writes and deletes are available before the first assembled line of a pass.
Evaluates the complete source expression using the context values.

entry.register-use: Query 0 for API/CPU/value masks, or 1 for a CPU ID in R1.

use.p: Allows callers to discover supported CPUs and future extensions.

entry.register-use: Message buffer address, or zero to query size.

use.p: Does not clear the saved diagnostic.

section.title: Error Messages
section.p: Module errors report invalid handles, CPU IDs, pass state, values, memory and assembly operations. Backend failures are translated to the assembly error while their original classifier and message remain available through Assembler_LastError.

section.title: Examples
section.extended-example: handle = Assembler_Create(ASSEMBLER_CPU_6502) Assembler_BeginPass(handle, first, output, capacity, address) Assembler_AssembleLine(handle, " LDA #value", opt) if Assembler_BeginPass(handle, second, output, capacity, address) != 0 replay every source line Assembler_Destroy(handle)
